problem_statement: themewagon/iPortfolio is a static single-page Bootstrap 5 portfolio, here rebranded for Marlowe Ashcroft, a one-person kinetic-sculpture and clockwork-mechanism studio. The site owner wants the studio's collection vocabulary (Automata / Orreries / Wall pieces / Studies) to read as a consistent, first-class part of the page, so a shared "Studio index" rail was added that repeats the same collection taxonomy in the studio-log band, again in the stats section, and once more in the footer. The Portfolio section's existing collection filter was also given a live text readout (id="portfolio-readout") so that choosing a collection echoes the selection back as "Now viewing: <collection>". Three regressions shipped together and must be repaired as one coherent piece of work. (1) MOBILE OVERFLOW: on a 390px phone the home page scrolls sideways because the "From the studio log" band's metric row is a fixed-width, non-wrapping flex row (#studio-log .studio-log-row { flex-wrap:nowrap; width:760px } with each tile min-width:170px) in assets/css/main.css, so the row cannot shrink below ~760px and pushes the document wider than the viewport. (2) INCONSISTENT SHARED RAIL: the Studio index rail must appear in all three sections (studio-log, stats, footer) with the quiet iPortfolio look; a version that drops the rail from some sections, or restyles it into an off-palette dark slab, breaks the site-wide consistency the owner asked for. (3) STALE FILTER READOUT: clicking a collection filter must update the portfolio-readout text to name the chosen collection; a handler that only recolors the active filter but leaves the readout stale is broken. Repair all three so the 390px home page has no horizontal overflow, the Studio index rail is present and on-brand in every section, and the collection filter's readout tracks the selection, while keeping the rest of the iPortfolio layout, navigation, sections, imagery and footer intact.
required_content: The 390px mobile home page must have no horizontal overflow: the document must not be wider than the viewport (the sideways scroll must be gone).
The shared "Studio index" rail (text "Studio index", the four collection chips) must appear in the studio-log band, the stats section, AND the footer — all three sections, not just one.

The Studio index rail must keep the quiet iPortfolio look (near-white surface, hairline border, rounded corners, green collection chips), consistent with the reference; it must not be restyled into an off-palette dark slab.

Clicking a Portfolio collection filter must update the live readout (id="portfolio-readout") to "Now viewing: <collection>" (e.g. clicking Orreries yields "Now viewing: Orreries"); the readout must track the current selection, not stay stale on "Now viewing: All".

The "From the studio log" band keeps its four metric tiles and heading; the About/Skills/Resume/Portfolio/Services/Testimonials/Contact sections, the section navigation and the footer stay intact and reachable.
No new console errors or failed network requests may be introduced; the page must stay runtime-clean.
design_constraints: Preserve iPortfolio's visual language: dark profile sidebar, light content sections, Bootstrap 5 grid, bootstrap-icons, AOS reveal, the studio-log tile look, and the quiet near-white/green Studio index rail treatment.
Fix the mobile overflow in the studio-log band's CSS so the metric row wraps or shrinks to fit narrow viewports instead of staying pinned to a fixed width wider than the phone.
Keep the Studio index rail present in all three sections with the shared rail chrome; the rail markup and text are identical everywhere — only its site-wide presence and on-brand styling matter.
Wire the collection filter readout so a click re-renders the portfolio-readout text to the selected collection; the terminal state after a click must name the chosen collection.
Do not introduce external stock images, remote fonts, or third-party embeds; the site is served as static files offline.
state_constraints: desktop_home / mobile_home / tablet_home capture the rebranded masthead and studio-log band; at 390px the baseline fixed-width row forces the document wider than the viewport.
desktop_studio_log / mobile_studio_log scroll to the studio-log band where the Studio index rail is graded for visual fidelity and mobile overflow.
desktop_stats_regression / desktop_footer_regression confirm the shared Studio index rail is repeated in the stats and footer sections (cross-section consistency).
desktop_portfolio_initial captures the Portfolio collection filter before any click (readout shows "Now viewing: All").
desktop_portfolio_filter clicks the "Orreries" collection filter; the terminal readout must update to "Now viewing: Orreries".
desktop_about anchors the About section for the untouched-layout regression check.

change_completion: The 390px mobile home page no longer overflows horizontally.
The Studio index rail is present in the studio-log, stats and footer sections, and the collection-filter readout names the selected collection after a click.
design_consistency: The Studio index rail keeps the near-white/green iPortfolio look across all three sections rather than a collapsed dark slab.
The repaired studio-log band keeps the iPortfolio tile styling and Bootstrap rhythm; changes stay scoped to the band CSS, the rail chrome, and the filter-readout wiring.
regression: Static site still serves without a custom dev server; the portfolio sections, nav and footer are unchanged and reachable.
No new console errors or failed network requests are introduced.
responsive: 390px home has no horizontal overflow, and the metric tiles wrap or shrink to fit.
Desktop and tablet home layouts remain unaffected.

author_notes: Repo-grounded static Bootstrap Repair/regression_continuity task hardened to L4. A shallow non-fix fails FOUR orthogonal gates: D6 no_horizontal_overflow (fixed-width non-wrapping studio-log row still overflows 390px), D2 dom_assertions cross-section (Studio index rail missing from stats+footer), D3 visual_regression (rail restyled into an off-palette dark slab), and D4 interaction_assertions (collection filter click leaves the portfolio-readout stale). The original-defect baseline fails D6/D2/D3 but keeps the correct readout wiring so it passes D4 (leg-orthogonal). Content and DOM text are identical across legs; the only leg-varying files are assets/css/main.css, assets/js/studio-index.js and the rail placement in index.html.
